articles.title: Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Blue Jays emerge as Tarik Skubal suitors as market for top MLB free agent takes shape
articles.summary: "It's very clear that it's a dominant and strong Sku-bull market," agent Scott Boras said, offering one of his signature free-agency puns.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — As the MLB general managers meetings got underway Tuesday , speculation started to ramp up regarding the offseason's top free agent, Tarik Skubal. This year, the 29-year-old superstar left-hander is in a tier of his own.

Skubal is not only this offseason's No. 1 free agent , but he's also the best starting pitcher available by far. While Freddy Peralta, Michael King, Trevor Rogers, Clay Holmes and others are strong rotation options for contenders, none of them is the clear-cut ace that Skubal is.

"It's very clear that it's a dominant and strong Sku-bull market," agent Scott Boras said Wednesday in Las Vegas, offering one of his signature free-agency puns.

"In the deep waters of talent treasure, there's no time to come up for air. Teams have filled their tanks, and they're all clearly ready for the Skubal dive," he continued.

As usual, several MLB teams are looking for starting pitching on this year's free-agent market, but because of the price the two-time Cy Young Award winner is expected to command, two teams have emerged as the early front-runners for Skubal's services: the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets.

The Dodgers, who acquired Skubal from Detroit ahead of the August trade deadline , have a robust assortment of starting pitching options already in-house, including Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Justin Wrobleski, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Even so, it's clear the free-agent ace made an impact while in Dodger blue.

"He was awesome getting to know [this season]. Fit in great in the clubhouse," Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said. "Obviously, we know what kind of pitcher he is. For us, it's understanding what this all looks like, what does our team need, what does the contract look like. We know we love the player. We love the human. Now we kind of have to play out to see what all that looks like."

Despite the Dodgers' stated interest in bringing him back, the Mets are viewed as the favorites to land Skubal. New York lacks a clear ace to pair with right-hander Nolan McLean at the top of their rotation, and after things did not go as hoped for Peralta in Queens in 2026 , Skubal represents a chance at redemption for the Mets this offseason.

New York has also shown a willingness to pay at the top of the market under owner Steve Cohen, most notably with the team's decision to make Juan Soto the highest-paid player in the history of professional sports . Still, since the arrival of president of baseball operations David Stearns, the Mets haven't come to terms on a long-term deal with a starting pitcher.

"Every situation is unique. It's been well-publicized, even since I've been here, we've engaged in extremely long-term negotiations for [starting] pitchers," Stearns said. "We will do so again, but [the] situation matters, the specific circumstance matters. We do have to look at every individual pitcher on a case-by-case basis."

Stearns went on to discuss the Mets' status as an appealing free-agent destination.

"I think it starts with our ownership and organizational commitment to winning," he said. "And since Steve and Alex Cohen have bought the team, they've spared no expense to do everything they possibly can to to win, to demonstrate to players, to demonstrate to players' families, that this is a desirable location, and when players come here and they see that, I think it becomes a very attractive place to play."

While the Dodgers and Mets will dominate much of the speculation around the two-time Cy Young Award winner, one of the biggest questions over the next several weeks is which teams are actually in position to acquire Skubal, given his price point?

It has been reported that Skubal and Boras are planning to meet with the San Diego Padres and the Toronto Blue Jays in the coming weeks, but the sheer size of Skubal's desired contract will limit the number of legitimate suitors.

Over the past few years, it has come to be expected that Skubal will look to top the average annual value record of $43.3 million set by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander as well as the total pitcher contract value record of $325 million set by Yoshinobu Yamamoto in 2023.

"The rarity of the [Greg] Madduxes, the [Randy] Johnsons, the [Hunter] Browns, the [Gerrit] Coles. When you go back and look at the [Max] Scherzers, all these true No. 1 [Barry] Zitos, they've all led to world championships," Boras said. "That's kind of what the teams are about. … If we live over a 30- or 40-year period, we might have less than 10 of these aces that are capable of winning multiple Cy Youngs. And what that means is having … an opportunity to win a championship."

Even with the collective bargaining agreement set to expire in less than three weeks, Boras doesn't sound like he feels any pressure to hurry to get a deal done for Skubal. Five years ago, the super-agent agreed to contracts worth a combined $500 million for free-agent clients Corey Seager and Marcus Semien right before the 2021 CBA expiration.

With baseball's economics a much bigger talking point this time around, we'll see if he can get a mega-deal done before the deadline once again.

articles.title: Yankees' Cam Schlittler Wins AL Cy Young 2026 Awards, Full Voting Results
articles.summary: New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler's breakout 2026 season earned him the American League Cy Young award.
articles.body:
New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler's breakout 2026 season earned him the American League Cy Young award.

Schlittler finished ahead of fellow finalists Dylan Cease and Parker Messick to receive the award on Wednesday.

A midseason call-up in 2025, Schlittler flashed ace potential as a rookie with a 2.96 ERA and 84 strikeouts in 73 innings.

This season saw Schlittler live up to the promise of his first year. He led the AL with a 1.95 ERA in 193.2 innings and earned his first All-Star nod.

Schlittler became the first Yankees starter with a sub-2.00 ERA in a season since Ron Guidry in 1978. It was also the lowest ERA for an AL starting pitcher since Justin Verlander in 2022.

As the Yankees offense struggled for long stretches of the season with Aaron Judge injured, Schlittler always gave them a chance to win when he was on the mound.

The right-hander allowed one earned run or fewer in 21 of his 33 starts, including each of his final nine outings in the regular season.

Schlittler is the seventh pitcher in Yankees history to win the Cy Young award and the first since Gerrit Cole in 2023. He joins a group that also includes Guidry, Bob Turley, Whitey Ford, Sparky Lyle and Roger Clemens.

articles.body:
Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski and New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler earned some hardware Wednesday for their breakout 2026 seasons.

Schlittler won the 2026 American League Cy Young award and finished ahead of fellow finalists Dylan Cease and Parker Messick. Misiorowski captured the 2026 National League Cy Young award by defeating fellow finalists Chris Sale and Cristopher Sánchez.

They weren't the only pitchers to win awards Wednesday, as Louis Varland of the Toronto Blue Jays won the American League Reliever of the Year. San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller took home the same award for the National League.

As for Schlittler, he flashed ace potential as a midseason call-up in 2025 with a 2.96 ERA and 84 strikeouts in 73 innings.

This season saw Schlittler live up to the promise of his first year. He led the AL with a 1.95 ERA in 193.2 innings and earned his first All-Star nod.

Schlittler became the first Yankees starter with a sub-2.00 ERA in a season since Ron Guidry in 1978. It was also the lowest ERA for an AL starting pitcher since Justin Verlander in 2022.

As the Yankees offense struggled for long stretches of the season with Aaron Judge injured, Schlittler always gave them a chance to win when he was on the mound.

The right-hander allowed one earned run or fewer in 21 of his 33 starts, including each of his final nine outings in the regular season.

Schlittler is the seventh pitcher in Yankees history to win the Cy Young award and the first since Gerrit Cole in 2023. He joins a group that also includes Guidry, Bob Turley, Whitey Ford, Sparky Lyle and Roger Clemens.

It was quite the year for Misiorowski as well.

After showing tremendous promise in 66 innings as a rookie in 2025, Misiorowski leveled up to reach historic heights this season. He led MLB with a 1.80 ERA, 252 strikeouts, 4.9 hits allowed per nine innings and 13.0 strikeouts per nine innings.

Misiorowski set a new MLB record for fewest hits allowed per nine innings, breaking the previous mark of 5.07 by Ferdie Schupp in 1916. There were no shortage of historic stats from Misiorowski in 2026, including lowest batting average against (.157) and third-best WHIP (0.802) ever. He joined Pedro Martinez in 2000 and Justin Verlander in 2019 as the only pitchers with at least 250 strikeouts and a WHIP of 0.8 or lower in a season.

Misiorowski also broke the velocity barrier in ways that no pitcher has since pitch-tracking began in MLB in 2008.

The NL Cy Young was Misiorowski's to lose for most of the season, and he never gave voters a reason to strongly consider anyone else. He is the fourth Brewers pitcher to win the Cy Young, joining Rollie Fingers (1981), Pete Vuckovich (1982) and Corbin Burnes (2021).

Misiorowski is the first pitcher since Verlander in 2022 to win both a World Series title and Cy Young award in the same season.

articles.title: Cam Schlittler unanimously wins 2026 AL Cy Young Award after historic season for Yankees
articles.summary: Schlittler posted a 14-6 record and a 1.95 ERA in his second big-league season.
articles.body:
New York Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler unanimously won the 2026 AL Cy Young Award. He received all 30 first-place votes from the BBWAA, the league announced Wednesday.

Schlittler started 33 games for New York this season, posting a 14-6 record and a 1.95 ERA. He struck out 239 batters across 193 2/3 innings.

The 25-year-old's ERA was the lowest in the American League and second-lowest in MLB, with only Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski (1.80) besting him. Schlittler was tied with Dylan Cease for third in the majors in strikeouts, behind Misiorowski (252) and Gavin Williams (248).

Schlittler led the AL in pitching WAR (6.2) and opponent on-base percentage (.244) while posting the third-lowest ERA in Yankees franchise history , trailing only Spud Chandler (1.64 in 1943) and Ron Guidry (1.74 in 1978). Guidry won the AL Cy Young Award in 1978.

The Yankees starter was a finalist for the award along with Toronto's Cease and Cleveland Guardians starter Parker Messick. Cease had the most second-place votes at 22, ahead of seven for Messick and one for Tampa Bay Rays ace Drew Rasmussen.

After watching Schlittler all season, Yankees manager Aaron Boone was confident his ace would win.

"He's going to win the Cy Young. I think he's just continued to get better year in and year out. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch when he got called up last year. "He's been the best pitcher in the league. When you have that going all year at the top of your rotation, that's massive. And that's what he's been."

"He's going to win the Cy Young. I think he's just continued to get better year in and year out. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch when he got called up last year.

"He's been the best pitcher in the league. When you have that going all year at the top of your rotation, that's massive. And that's what he's been."

Schlittler was drafted in the seventh round of the 2022 MLB Draft. At the start of the 2025 season, the right-hander was with New York's Double-A affiliate in Somerset.

After injuries to other starters in the rotation, the Yankees promoted Schittler. He made his MLB debut on July 9, 2025, and earned a win over the Seattle Mariners. In his debut, the righty allowed three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings and struck out seven.

Overall, Schlittler made 14 starts as a rookie, posting a 4-3 record and a 2.96 ERA. He then stunned the Red Sox in the playoffs , striking out 12 in a wild-card victory.

Barring an extension, Schlittler has one more pre-arbitration year left, then three years of arbitration. He made $801,000 in 2026, per Spotrac .

articles.title: AL Cy Young Award: The Yankees' Cam Schlittler was the undisputed answer
articles.summary: The 25-year-old righty dominated the American League in his first full season as a a major leaguer.
articles.body:
No team has spent more aggressively on starting pitching in free agency than the New York Yankees. In MLB history, only 17 starters have signed free-agent deals worth more than $150 million, and five of those were with the Yankees (no other franchise has signed more than two). Three of those pitchers — Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón, with contracts totaling more than $700 million — remain entrenched in New York's rotation today.

On Wednesday, it was announced that the seventh AL Cy Young Award winner in Yankees history is not one of these highly paid hurlers, but rather, one they gave a $205,000 bonus after selecting him in the seventh round of the 2022 MLB Draft. That's 25-year-old right-hander Cam Schlittler, who received all 30 first-place votes from the BBWAA electorate , beating fellow finalists Dylan Cease of Toronto and Parker Messick of Cleveland. Schlittler joins Cole and Roger Clemens as Yankees' Cy Youngs this century and is the youngest Yankee ever to take home the award and the franchise's first homegrown starter to win since Ron Guidry in 1978.

This was one heck of a statement for Schlittler to make in his first full year as a major leaguer. Although he exhausted his rookie eligibility in 2025 with a stellar showing down the stretch and a spectacular outing against the Red Sox in October , several questions loomed as Schlittler embarked on his first full season in the Yankees' rotation in 2026. Would his overwhelmingly fastball-forward arsenal hold up, or would a more diverse assortment of pitches be required to keep hitters guessing? Could he improve his walk rate, which climbed above 10% last year? What about his susceptibility to airborne contact — Schlittler's 36.4% ground-ball rate ranked in the 20th percentile as a rookie — especially pitching in Yankee Stadium?

To be clear, there was mostly optimism surrounding Schlittler entering this season. At the same time, it felt like the dozen strikeouts he recorded over eight scoreless innings against the rival Red Sox last October might have amplified the hype beyond realistic expectations. As it turned out, that hype was wholly justified. Schlittler began his 2026 season with two scoreless outings in San Francisco and Seattle totaling 11 ⅔ innings with just three hits allowed and 15 strikeouts. With that, the tone was set.

Over the next six months, rarely did Schlittler stumble, finishing the season with a 1.95 ERA and 239 strikeouts across 193 ⅔ innings pitched. He delivered another postseason gem against Boston (6 ⅓ IP, 2 H, 0 R, 1 BB, 10 K) before a more mediocre showing against Tampa Bay in the ALDS contributed to New York's early October exit. The body of work amassed during the regular season left no doubt about who would collect the hardware. Schlittler's 1.95 ERA was the lowest by a qualified Yankee since the aforementioned Guidry in his sensational debut campaign nearly 50 years ago (1.74). Before Guidry, you have to go all the way back to Spud Chandler in 1943 (1.64) to find a lower mark.

Chandler won AL MVP that year, and while Schlittler won't be winning that award when it is announced Thursday, it's reasonable to suggest that he deserved consideration as a finalist. His 7.0 bWAR ranked second in the AL behind only Tigers rookie sensation Kevin McGonigle (7.1), and his 6.2 fWAR ranked third behind Bobby Witt Jr. (7.0) and presumptive MVP Yordan Alvarez (6.8). And somehow, Schlittler's sensational surface-level run prevention almost undersells how consistent he was at throwing up zeroes.

Schlittler made 33 regular-season starts, and he allowed one or zero earned runs in 25 of them. That's not just the most such outings by a pitcher this year (by far — Jacob Misiorowski was second with 20); it's tied with 1963 Sandy Koufax for the most in a single season since integration (excluding openers). Tied for second on that list, with 24, is Koufax in 1966 and Bob Gibson in 1968. Decent company!

Watch even a few innings from Schlittler, and it's not difficult to understand why scoring against him is so difficult. The 6-foot-6 righty attacks relentlessly with elite velocity via three different fastball variations — 44% four-seam, 26% cutter, 19% sinker — proving that pure dominance can be possible with minimal breaking ball or off-speed usage. Of course, the Red Sox learned the hard way in October that his curveball is pretty dang good, too.

Crucially, in 2026, Schlittler also made strides with his command and keeping the ball in the ballpark, cutting his walk rate to 6.4% (13th-lowest among 46 qualified starters) and upping his ground-ball rate to 43.2% (above league-average). He surrendered just 16 home runs in the regular season — 11 of them solo shots — which equates to a 0.74 HR/9 that was sixth-lowest in MLB.

Put it all together, and any and all suspense was eliminated leading up to Wednesday's Cy Young announcement. Schlittler was the undisputed answer.

Schlittler's journey from being drafted as a late-round pick to being unanimously named the best pitcher in his league is a remarkable testament to the Yankees' developmental aptitude on the mound, a valuable organizational trait that works brilliantly in tandem with the organization's deep pockets enabling the acquisition of impact arms in free agency.

With his career still just beginning, Schlittler represents the ultimate success story of a talented, but raw, young pitcher who had the kind of physical frame that hints at significant upside with the right instruction and coaching — and one who landed with exactly the right team to maximize that potential.

articles.title: MLB awards 2026: Full list of finalists, winners for MVP, Rookie of the Year, Cy Young and more
articles.summary: Here's a look at who won each of MLB's top awards in 2026.
articles.body:
With Major League Baseball heading into the offseason, the league has one final piece of business left from 2026: the end-of-season awards.

Throughout the week, MLB will announce winners of prestigious awards like MVP, Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year, giving the season's best players the praise they deserve. In some cases, the awards feel wrapped already, but there are a few close races that came down to the bitter end.

In the past two years, Aaron Judge, Shohei Ohtani , Tarik Skubal, and Paul Skenes dominated this time of year, but for the most part, there is some new blood that rose to prominence in 2026. As a result, many of this year's finalists are possible first-time winners after they broke out with impressive performances.

While SN's awards — which are voted on by players, managers and GMs — were previously announced, here's a look at who won MLB's awards in 2026, as voted by the BBWAA.

Cam Schlittler, Yankees : In a rotation full of aces, Cam Schlittler rose above the rest to take the mantle as the best pitcher on the Yankees. The right-hander showed what he can do last season, and he was even better in 2026 with a league-leading 1.95 ERA and 7.0 bWAR in 193.2 innings pitched. What made Schlittler's performance even more impressive is that he did all this in New York, where so many players fold under the pressure. A Cy Young win makes Schlittler the seventh Yankee to win the award and puts his name up there with some elite company.

Dylan Cease, Blue Jays : Cease's first year with the Blue Jays after signing a lengthy contract couldn't have gone any better. The veteran put up a 2.40 ERA in 29 games, continuing to provide durability and taking the mantle as the ace of the Toronto staff. It wasn't a career-best season, as Cease was the Cy Young runner-up in 2022 with a 2.20 ERA for the White Sox, but he did reach a career high with 239 strikeouts in the season. While the Blue Jays took a step back in 2026, Cease did everything in his power to keep the team afloat through the Summer.

Parker Messick, Guardians : Messick was the best rookie pitcher in baseball this season, as his 2.56 ERA and his 6.3 bWAR vaulted him to the top of the Guardians rotation. Messick flashed last year in seven games, and he only built on that when he threw 186.1 innings in his first full season for a Cleveland team that once again won the AL West. Messick was unable to unseat his two competitors for the Cy Young, but this shouldn't be the last time that he competes for this award in his career.

Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers : "The Miz" took the world by storm in 2025 when he brought his elite fastball to the majors, but he still hadn't yet learned how to pitch. That changed in 2026 as Misiorowski led baseball's best team to a title while leading the majors with a 1.80 ERA. Misiorowski's ability to not only light up the radar gun, but do so on a consistent basis makes him rare, even in an era with so many flamethrowers in the league. The question is more about how many Cy Youngs he will win as he enters the prime of his career.

Chris Sale, Braves : The 2024 Cy Young winner continued his rejuvenated career with the Braves, throwing to a 2.16 ERA in 27 starts this year. That is the third-best ERA in Sale's storied career, and second-best since he became a full-time starter in 2012. At 37 years old, Sale continues to build on what is now a Hall-of-Fame career by leading the Atlanta staff, as he rose to the occasion against the league's best teams throughout the season.

Cristopher Sanchez, Phillies : Cristopher Sanchez was the runner-up in this award last season, and he didn't miss a beat with a second consecutive dominant campaign. Sanchez posted a 2.91 ERA in 207 innings while leading the league in wins, with 18, and starts, with 33. For the second consecutive season, Sanchez's 8.1 bWAR led the National League, and this time it came with a career high in strikeouts. Sanchez continues to be a coup for a Phillies team that acquired him in a minor deal and helped develop him in a major way.

Will Venable, White Sox : Last year, Venable took over a White Sox team that lost 121 games, but it took him just two seasons to lead Chicago back to the playoffs. That turnaround is among the best in MLB history, as Venable brought a young team together and competed all year long for the AL Central division title. Simply making the playoffs is impressive, even if it was as a Wild Card, as the White Sox do not have many playoff berths in their long history.

Kevin Cash, Rays : No one expected the Rays to be the best team in the American League in 2026, but it wasn't a total surprise with Cash at the helm. The two-time manager of the year once again led Tampa Bay to a season with 98 wins and an AL East crown, all while representing the AL in the World Series for the second time. With a second-place finish, he missed out on a list of nine other managers to win this award three times.

Chad Tracy, Red Sox : Tracy had a tall task when he took over the Red Sox from the fired Alex Cora, but he impressed all Summer. After a slow start, Tracy' club had the best winning streak of the season at 15-straight games, and no team was better from late June through July than Boston, which helped the team make it back to the playoffs. It earned Tracy a multi-year contract to stay in Boston moving forward as one of the game's rising young coaches.

Pat Murphy, Brewers : Murphy first three seasons as the Brewers' manager couldn't have gone any better. Milwaukee won the NL Central in the first two, then Murphy led the team to its first World Series title in 2026. In 2024 and 2025, Murphy became one of just two managers to win this award in each of his first two seasons, and another win makes history, as no manager has done it in his first three seasons.

Don Mattingly, Phillies : The Phillies fired Rob Thomson in April, hoping for a shakeup, and it was Mattingly who righted the ship and got the Phillies back on track. Managing Philadelphia comes with so much pressure and expectations, but that wasn't an issue for someone who played his entire career in New York. Mattingly led the Phillies to a Wild Card berth and was rewarded with a contract extension to make him the full-time manager moving forward.

Walt Weiss, Braves : The Braves moved on from Brian Snitker after an underwhelming 2025 season, but stayed in-house by promoting Weiss. A former Rockies manager, Weiss immediately hit the ground running and led Atlanta back to the top of the NL East with another division title despite dealing with injuries throughout the roster. Under Weiss, the Braves once again have World Series expectations in the future.

Kevin McGonigle, Tigers : McGonigle hit the ground running for the Tigers as no player in the American League had more plate appearances in 2026. The shortstop put up an .806 OPS with 18 home runs in his first MLB season, all while leading the AL with a 7.1 bWAR. Although Detroit had a disappointing season, McGonigle's immediate breakout proved he is a cornerstone piece for a team that needed that in the wake of the Tarik Skubal trade.

Parker Messick, Guardians : Messick is the only player nominated for two awards this year, a testament to his success as a rookie. He made two Game 1 starts for the Guardians, showing that Cleveland had the confidence in him to make big starts in the playoffs. With a 2.56 ERA and his 6.3 bWAR for the year, Messick became the latest Guardians pitcher to find himself at the top of the Cleveland rotation early in his career.

Payton Tolle, Red Sox : Tolle's first full season in the majors put him atop the Red Sox rotation, as he posted a 3.03 ERA in 26 games. What makes Tolles so special is his strikeout ability, producing 171 strikeouts in 148.2 innings pitched over the course of the year. Tolle also won the hearts of baseball fans with his approach to the game, not taking his work too seriously despite bringing a ton of passion. As Boston had the game's deepest rotation in the Summer, Tolle was the one who stood out.

Sal Stewart, Reds : Stewart is not the most well-rounded player in the league, but he did produce on offense for the Reds at an elite rate. Stewart set the record for most RBIs by a rookie in a single season with 112, and his 32 home runs were good enough to lead the Cincinnati offense. He also chipped in 15 stolen bases, a solid number for a player who primarily plays first base, and he made his first All-Star game in the process.

Carson Benge, Mets : Although the Mets had a miserable year, Benge was a bright spot that became a cornerstone in the outfield for years to come. The lefty hitter hit 20 home runs with 22 stolen bases in the season, all while producing a .282 batting average in the process. He also played elite defense in right field, showing off one of the game's best outfield arms time and time again. As the Mets continue to remake their team, Benge will become a stalwart.

JJ Wetherholt, Cardinals : Like McGonigle in Detroit, Wetherholt broke out with the Cardinals thanks to an all-around game that included offense, defense and baserunning. The middle infielder hit 17 home runs with 14 RBIs while playing strong defense at second base, but very well could've played every day at shortstop if the team needed him to do so. St. Louis was all about the youth in 2026, and Wetherholt was the perfect player to lead that charge.

AL MVP candidates (winner announced Nov. 12)

Yordan Alvarez, Astros : Alvarez had a career year in 2026, reaching over 40 home runs for the first time in his career while leading the league with a .316 batting average and a 1.033 OPS. Had it not been for Pete Alonso's 43 homers, Alvarez may have even won the triple crown award. The designated hitter was finally healthy for a full season, playing in 158 games and almost taking 700 plate appearances. While designated hitters are rarely in play to win the MVP, this shows just how special of a hitter that Alvarez is.

Junior Caminero, Rays :No player in the American League has more home runs than Caminero over the last two seasons, totaling 87 long balls. This year, though, Caminero showed improved patience at the plate as he made his second consecutive All-Star game, continuing to grow as a young slugger. It helps that the Rays were the best team in the American League, with Caminero being Tampa Bay's most fearsome hitter at the plate for 162 games. Caminero could also make history as the Rays' first MVP award winner.

Bobby Witt Jr., Royals : No player was hurt more by Aaron Judge's MVP dominance in 2024 and 2025 than Witt, who had two MVP-caliber seasons in those two years. In 2026, though, Witt's offensive numbers took a slight dip, but he stole 45 bases for the first time since 2023 and continued his production as one of, if not the best, defensive shortstops in the game. Witt is a true five-tool player, with strength all around the diamond, and it feels like a matter of time before he takes home an MVP award.

NL MVP candidates (winner announced Nov. 12)

Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs : Overtaking Shohei Ohtani as the MVP favorite required a special season, and that's exactly what PCA provided in 2026. The Cubs center fielder led all of baseball with 45 home runs and had the best OPS in the National League at .943, all while stealing 41 bases and playing elite defense in center field. Crow-Armstrong's 9.8 bWAR also led the league, putting his season in the same tier as Mike Trout, Mookie Betts, and Aaron Judge had in years past. An MVP win would make Crow-Armstrong the third all-time with a 40-40 season, joining Ohtani and Ronald Acuna Jr.

Shohei Ohtani, Dodgers : From 2021-25, Ohtani won four MVP awards by wowing the baseball world with his pitching, hitting, and baserunning. This year, however, injuries limited Ohtani's output, as he only pitched in half a season and had his lowest home run total in a 162-game season since 2019. It's a testament to Ohtani's success as a two-way player that he is even a finalist for the MVP award once again, as no player in baseball can do as much on the field as Ohtani can.

Brice Turang, Brewers : Turang represents the World Series champion Brewers in MVP voting after he had his best season as a big-leaguer. The second baseman had career highs in home runs, RBIs, and OPS, but it's his baserunning and defense that truly separates him from the rest. Turang put up a 7.3 bWAR this season despite totaling just 21 home runs, which shows how much value he brings on the margins. Very few people expected Turang to ever compete for MVP awards, but his value for the Brewers cannot be overstated.

articles.title: Yankees’ Cam Schlittler Wins 2026 Cy Young Award

articles.body:
The annual Cy Young award winner was announced for the 2026 season. New York Yankees right-handed starting pitcher Cam Schlittler takes the award, putting up a phenomenal performance this year.

Yankees' Cam Schlittler Wins 2026 Cy Young Award

The Yankees' main driving force in the rotation this season was Schlittler. Even with Gerrit Cole returning to play mid-season, Schlittler was looked upon as the ace. He was elite in many ways with striking dominance on the mound.

This was the right-hander's first full season in the Major Leagues, after being brought in late last season. Schlittler finished a solid season with a league-leading WAR at 7.0. He finished with a 14-6 win-loss record and a league-leading 1.95 ERA in 33 regular season starts.

Schlittler threw 193 and ⅔ innings, allowing 129 hits, 42 earned runs, and only 16 home runs. The ace-starter struck out an impressive 239 hitters, only walking 49 hitters while facing a total of 761 hitters.

Schlittler was far more dominant within his approach in his matchups. His velocity was high, sitting within the 99-101mph range, utilizing his junk options effectively. Although the Cy Young award particularly focuses on ERA, wins-loses, strikeouts, and more, his metrics were also impressive.

The Yankees ace has only scratched the surface of Major League Baseball. His first season as a Cy Young winner says a lot about what his career holds.

Previous awards from the minor leagues include in the 2024 Kevin Lawn Award, which recognizes the Yankees top minor league pitcher of the season. He was also named South Atlantic Pitcher of the year in High-A and postseason all-star.

The first ever Yankees Cy Young award winner was pitcher Bob Turley in 1958. In 1961, Whitey Ford won it, followed by Sparky Lyle in 1977, Ron Guidry in 1978, Rogers Clemens in 2001, and Gerrit Cole in 2023. The club had a ton of pitchers finishing second and third in the running.

With this award in conversation, there is a lot of positives in the future for the Yankees young ace. Schlittler has proven ability to be elite, and he's shown a great deal of dominance.

With the age of the rotation being a consideration, management may want to build around Schlittler, and create an elite young rotation. Schlittler will be the number one in the rotation moving forward. He'll need to put up another year of consistency to be that guy. 2027 will be another big season for the right-hander.

articles.title: Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler wins AL Cy Young Award
articles.summary: Cam Schlittler has won the American League Cy Young Award after posting a sub-2.00 ERA in his first full season in the major leagues.
articles.body:
Cam Schlittler won the American League Cy Young Award on Wednesday night, becoming the second New York Yankees pitcher to receive the honor in the last four years.

Gerrit Cole won it with the Yankees in 2023 before Tarik Skubal won the last two AL Cy Young Awards while pitching for Detroit. Cole had been the first Yankee to win the award since Roger Clemens in 2001.

The award is voted on by the Baseball Writers Association of America.

Schlittler, 25, went 14-6 with an AL-leading 1.95 ERA that ranked third in Yankees' history, behind Spud Chandler (1.64 in 1943) and Ron Guidry (1.74 in 1978). Schlittler's 239 strikeouts tied for second in the AL with Toronto's Dylan Cease, behind the 248 from Cleveland's Gavin Williams.

This was his first full season in the big leagues after he made his MLB debut in the summer of 2025.

The other two AL finalists were Cease and Cleveland's Parker Messick. Cease went 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA and was a Cy Young Award runner-up in 2022 with the Chicago White Sox. Messick went 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA and 193 strikeouts in 186 1/3 innings.

The NL Cy Young Award winner will be announced later Wednesday. Finalists are Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski, Philadelphia's Cristopher Sánchez and Atlanta's Chris Sale.

Misiorowski went 16-5 with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts in 174 2/3 innings. Sánchez was 18-7 with a 2.91 ERA and 231 strikeouts in 207 innings. Sale, who won the Cy Young Award in 2024, went 14-9 with a 2.16 ERA and 200 strikeouts in 162 2/3 innings.

The reliever of the year award winners in both leagues also will be announced Wednesday night. This marks the first year that the BBWAA has voted on a reliever of the year.

AL finalists are Tampa Bay's Bryan Baker, Toronto's Louis Varland and Cleveland's Cade Smith. NL finalists are Philadelphia's Jhoan Duran, Milwaukee's Trevor Megill and San Diego's Mason Miller.

articles.title: Louis Varland wins AL Reliever of the Year in tight race over Bryan Baker, Cade Smith
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Louis Varland won AL Reliever of the Year over Bryan Baker of the Tampa Bay Rays and Cade Smith of the Cleveland Guardians.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Louis Varland won the AL Reliever of the Year Award over fellow finalists Bryan Baker of the Tampa Bay Rays and Cade Smith of the Cleveland Guardians.

MLB announced Varland as the winner on Wednesday. He won in a tight race in which all three finalists received first-place votes.

Varland led the way with 16 out of 30 first-place votes and 146 points. Smith finished second in voting with seven first-place votes and 133 points, while Baker tallied six first-place votes and 111 points. Josh Hader of the Houston Astros secured the final first-place vote.

Varland secured the award on the heels of a career season on the mound as Toronto's closer. He finished the campaign with a 1.27 ERA and 1.000 WHIP with 97 strikeouts and 23 walks. His 35 saves were tied for the fifth-most in baseball.

They were also the first of his career. In four prior seasons mostly spent with the Minnesota Twins, Varland split his time between starts and middle relief.

He began his career as a starter with 15 starts across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He started to transition to the bullpen in 2024 and was a full-time reliever by 2025.

The move to the bullpen proved to be an immediate fit as he posted a career-low 2.97 ERA across 72 2/3 innings with the Twins and the Blue Jays. Varland has posted ERAs of 7.61 and 4.63 in his previous two seasons.

The Blue Jays recognized his potential and handed him the closer role for 2026 in a move that paid off with Varland winning AL Reliever of the Year.

articles.title: Padres closer Mason Miller named unanimous NL Reliever of the Year after career-high 38 saves
articles.summary: Miller was tied for the NL lead in saves along with St. Louis' Riley O'Brien.
articles.body:
San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller has unanimously won the 2026 NL Reliever of the Year Award.

This is the first time the BBWAA has voted on this award, and it differs from the Trevor Hoffman Reliever of the Year Award.

Miller made 66 appearances for San Diego this season. He recorded a 1.67 ERA and 0.900 WHIP. He converted 38 of 41 save opportunities, with only three blown saves. Before 2026, Miller's season high was 28 saves in 2024, when he was still with the Athletics. His 38 saves in 2026 tied for the NL lead with St. Louis Cardinals closer Riley O'Brien.

The San Diego closer was a finalist for the award along with Milwaukee Brewers closer Trevor Megill and Philadelphia Phillies closer Jhoan Duran. Miller received all 30 first-place votes. Duran finished second, with 24 second-place votes.

Early in the 2026 season, Miller set the Padres' scoreless-innings record by throwing 34 2/3 consecutive innings without giving up a run, dating to the end of last season. That broke the record of 33 2/3 scoreless innings set by Cla Meredith during the 2006 season.

The Athletics drafted Miller in the third round of the 2021 MLB Draft. His rise to the majors was meteoric. The right-hander began the 2023 season with the franchise's Double-A affiliate. Miller started one game and was called up to Triple-A, where he made one start before moving on to the bigs.

In his first MLB season, the right-hander pitched in 10 games, starting six. Those are the only big-league games he has ever started, as Miller has come out of the bullpen ever since.

Over four seasons, Miller has pitched in 191 games with a 2.47 ERA. The closer has converted 88 saves out of 98 save attempts.

Miller was named an All-Star for the first time in 2024 and again in 2026. This is the first time he has led the league in saves, and this is his first personal award.

The 28-year-old has three more years of arbitration before he hits free agency.

articles.title: Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski unanimously wins NL Cy Young Award after record-setting, World Series-winning season
articles.summary: No pitcher had a better 2026 than Jacob Misiorowski.
articles.body:
Jacob Misiorowski broke fastball velocity records in 2026. He won a World Series title in 2026. And now he's the 2026 NL Cy Young Award winner.

The flame-throwing right-hander added the award for the season's top pitcher to his trophy case on Wednesday, beating finalists Cristopher Sánchez of the Philadelphia Phillies and Chris Sale of the Atlanta Braves .

The vote was unanimous, with Misiorowski receiving first-place votes from all 30 BBWAA voters. It is the second consecutive season in which the award has been unanimous, after Paul Skenes of the Pittsburgh Pirates did the same in 2025.

New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler also won the AL Cy Young Award unanimously over Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays and Parker Messick of the Cleveland Guardians . This is only the third time in the history of the award that both leagues have been unanimous, joining 2022 (Justin Verlander and Sandy Alcantara) and 1968 (Bob Gibson and Denny McLain).

Sánchez finished second, garnering 17 second-place votes. Sale received 11 second-place votes, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto of the Los Angeles Dodgers received the remaining two.

The margin by which Misiorowski won is of little surprise. No pitcher dominated the NL like he did this year, leading the league in ERA (1.80 in 174 2/3 innings), strikeouts (252), WHIP (.802), FIP (2.17) and batting average against (.157). That was before he posted a 1.89 ERA across four starts during Milwaukee's World Series run, which didn't factor into the award voting. (Votes are cast at the end of the regular season.)

Misiorowski's arm was a key part of a historic season for the Brewers, who won a franchise-record 103 games, then departed the list of MLB teams that have never won a World Series. He is the fourth Milwaukee pitcher to win a Cy Young, joining Corbin Burnes (2021), Pete Vuckovich (1982) and Rollie Fingers (1981). Vuckovich and Fingers won the AL version of the award.

Misiorowski has had all eyes on him since his first MLB start last year, when he showed up with a triple-digit fastball and began his big-league career with 11 straight no-hit innings . He had an up-and-down rookie year, but that now looks like just a warmup act for what happened in 2026.

A triple-digit fastball is only the start of Jacob Misiorowski's dominance

The previous record for the fastest pitch ever thrown by a starting pitcher (and tracked by MLB, going back to 2008) was set by Jordan Hicks in 2022, when he dialed his fastball up to 103.2 mph. Misiorowski broke that record on May 8 with a 103.6 mph pitch.

"The Miz" then proceeded to throw 107 more pitches of 103.2 mph or faster over the course of the 2026 season , regularly setting a new velocity standard for starting pitchers. He reached his peak on June 26, when he hit 105.5 mph . Only two pitches in MLB history have been tracked as faster, with both coming from Aroldis Chapman as a reliever.

Not only did Misiorowski throw harder than MLB has ever seen from a starter, but his 6-foot-7 frame and low arm angle also give him elite extension to the plate, so batters have even less time to react. And he commands his pitches well, with a huge spin rate. His fastball could very well be the best MLB has ever seen .

Oh, and he throws a slider in the 90s, too. Just imagine trying to hit this sequence.

With all that, it's no wonder Misiorowski did what he did in 2026.

The 2026 NL Cy Young race looked like it would be competitive for much of the first half, but it was a one-man race by the All-Star break, provided that Misiorowski stayed healthy. He did, and he ultimately started the final game of the MLB postseason.

Will Misiorowski stay healthy going forward, given how hard he throws? The history of flame-throwing starting pitchers is against him. Even so, what the 24-year-old did in his second MLB season will be remembered as special.

articles.title: NL Cy Young Award: Jacob Misiorowski was the clear choice, both statistically and narratively
articles.summary: The Brewers' flame-throwing ace was the pitching main character of the 2026 MLB season.
articles.body:
Milwaukee's twiggy flame-thrower earned the hardware by unanimous decision on Wednesday, securing all 30 first-place votes from selected members of the Baseball Writers' Association of America.

I was one of them. And frankly, this wasn't a difficult decision. Misiorowski made it so.

Across 174 2/3 innings in 2026, the 24-year-old Brewer posted a microscopic 1.80 ERA with 252 strikeouts, both league-leading marks. His 0.802 WHIP (walks plus hits per innings pitched) was the second-lowest single-season mark among hurlers with at least 30 starts since Walter Johnson in 1913. His 37.9% strikeout rate was the second-highest ever, behind only Gerrit Cole in 2019. Misiorowski became the first pitcher to make 30 starts and surrender fewer than 100 hits in a season, and he popped the lowest opponents' batting average in MLB history (.157).

There is a legitimate argument that over a full season, no starting pitcher has ever been as difficult to hit as Misiorowski was in 2026.

Heat, of course, was his not-so-secret sauce.

Miz's four-seam fastball sat at 100.6 mph, making him the first starter in the pitch-tracking era to average triple digits. He threw more pitches at or over 100 mph (1,115) than every other starting pitcher combined (669) and 960 more than Bubba Chandler in second place. Only 22 other starters even threw a pitch over 100 mph.

He was undeniable, staggering, unprecedented.

That meant Phillies southpaw Cristopher Sánchez finished second for the second consecutive year. The case for Sánchez over Miz — one I entertained as a thought experiment — revolves around availability and bad luck. First, the bulk: Philly's ace threw 32 1/3 more innings than Milwaukee's and made three more starts (33 to 30). Sánchez delivered 25 starts of at least six innings; Misiorowski had just 18. Remove a cataclysmic, nine-earned-run stinker on July 7 from Sánchez's ledger, and his season ERA plummets from 2.91 to 2.56.

Sánchez was also the victim of some incredibly unfortunate batted ball luck. His opposing batting average on balls in play was a sky-high .336, compared to Misiorowski's .227. Miz's microscopic figure is partially a product of his preposterously overpowering stuff inducing mountains of weak contact. It's also a result of Milwaukee's sensational defense and positioning. The inverse was true for Sánchez, who had to overcome one of the game's worst fielding units.

Philadelphia finished 2026 with minus-51 defensive runs saved, tied for last with the Athletics in MLB. Its regular infield was particularly porous, with shortstop Trea Turner, third baseman Alec Bohm and first baseman Bryce Harper all grading out poorly by advanced metrics. That was an awful match for the sinker-heavy Sánchez, whose 57.7% groundball rate led qualified starters. That unsavory combo yielded more weak base hits, more baserunners and more runs than would've been the case if, say, Sánchez had the Brewers' defense and positioning behind him.

And yet, as compelling as that dynamic was, it didn't come close to bridging the statistical chasm between Sánchez and Misiorowski. The storytelling heft of Misiorowski's year helped, too: An ascension from a sushi-raw rookie freak show to one of the most dominant pitching seasons ever. Notably, award voting happens before the playoffs, meaning that Milwaukee's October run played no part in Miz's victory, but his role in propelling the Brewers to the best record in the sport did factor into my thinking.

In the end, the decision for the top spot was clear. Misiorowski was the pitching main character of the 2026 MLB season, both statistically and narratively. He is now one of the most recognizable figures in the sport, a fire-breathing unicorn on the mound.

The rest of my NL Cy Young ballot was also pretty straightforward. Sánchez beat Sale for second, even though Sale had a much lower ERA because he threw only 162 2/3 innings. Atlanta's lefty ace edged out Yamamoto for me on strikeout-to-walk rate. Yamamoto punched out 25.7% of hitters, while Sale struck out 30.9% and walked fewer batters.

Jesús Luzardo slotted in the final spot, though I heavily considered San Diego closer Mason Miller, who crafted one of the more show-stopping relief seasons in recent memory. In the end, though, Miller's relatively pedestrian finish (4.61 ERA across his final 12 outings) and the incredibly high bar for reliever value pushed him off my ballot.

1. Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers 2. Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies 3. Chris Sale, Braves 4. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers 5. Jesús Luzardo, Phillies

Houston Astros star Yordan Alvarez won the 2026 Edgar Martínez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award on Wednesday night.

Alvarez became the first Astros player to ever receive the honor.

Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani had previously won the award in each of the past five years to tie an MLB record , although Alvarez ended the streak following an impressive 2026 campaign that also made him a finalist for American League MVP.

Alvarez won the first batting title of his career by hitting a league-leading .316 during the regular season. His .432 on-base percentage and 1.033 OPS also represented the best marks in the majors.

In 158 games, Alvarez racked up 34 doubles, 42 home runs, 106 RBI and 109 walks.

While the 29-year-old has been a crucial piece of Houston's lineup throughout his career, his 2026 season was particularly impressive considering hand and ankle injuries limited him to just 48 games played in 2025.

Alvarez took home plenty of hardware on Wednesday night, as he was also named AL Comeback Player of the Year.

He earned the Hank Aaron Award as the best offensive performer in the American League and was selected to the All-MLB first-team as well.

articles.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Yordan Alvarez Win 2026 MLB Hank Aaron Awards for AL and NL
articles.summary: No surprises here.
articles.body:
After dominant seasons, Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez and Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong were named the AL and NL Hank Aaron Award winners on Wednesday.

The award is given to the top offensive performer from each league, as decided by fans and a panel of Hall of Fame players. And with both Alvarez and Crow-Armstrong expected to win their respective MVP awards, neither selection came as much of a surprise.

Alvarez, 29, led the American League in batting average (.316), was tied for second in homers (42), was second in RBI (106), tied for third in runs (105), was tied for fourth in doubles (34), was second in wins-above replacement (6.8) among position players and led the league in OPS (1.033).

While players like Pete Alonso (43 homers, 113 RBI, .884 OPS) and Junior Caminero (42 homers, 101 RBI, .885 OPS) had fantastic seasons, there was no denying Alvarez.

Crow-Armstrong, 24, hit .280 and tied for first in the National League in homers (45), was first in runs (119), third in RBI (107), tied for fifth in tripes (eight), was first in OPS (.943) and first in position-player WAR (9.8).

Some of his MVP-worthy impact is absolutely related to his fantastic defense, but he was easily the NL's most impactful bat this season as well and a worthy winner of the Hank Aaron Award.

Other players who made a case included Kyle Schwarber (45 homers, 97 RBI, .857 OPS) and James Wood (30 homers, 77 RBI, 106 runs, 21 stolen bases, .891 OPS).

The All-MLB teams for the 2026 season were officially announced on Wednesday night.

Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski, Baltimore Orioles first baseman Pete Alonso and San Diego Padres outfielder Fernando Tatis Jr. headlined the first-team roster.

Crow-Armstrong put together an impressive 2026 campaign, earning his second consecutive All-Star nod before he was selected as a National League MVP Award finalist .

He finished with 45 home runs in the regular season, tied for the most among all MLB players. Crow-Armstrong also racked up 31 doubles, 41 stolen bases and 107 RBI while posting a .280/.372/.570 slash line.

Misiorowski helped lead the Brewers to their first World Series title in franchise history and earned NL Cy Young Award recognition on Wednesday.

In 30 starts, he compiled a 16-5 record to go along with a 1.80 ERA and 0.802 WHIP. Misiorowski amassed 252 strikeouts, the most in the majors.

Alonso showcased his power at the plate throughout his first year on the Orioles, as his 43 homers ranked No. 1 in the American League. He also recorded 24 doubles and 113 RBI.

Alonso particularly thrived to close out the season, hitting .308 with a 1.051 OPS over his final 50 games played.

Tatis remained an key piece of the Padres' lineup as they advanced to the NLDS for the second time in three years.

Across 159 appearances during the regular season, Tatis slashed .289/.358/.470 while tallying 25 home runs, 32 doubles, 38 stolen bases and 83 RBI. His 181 total hits were the third-most in the National League.

articles.title: Yankees vs. Mets Battle for Former All-Star Revealed in New MLB Free Agency Rumors
articles.summary: With both the New York Yankees and New York Mets searching for infield help this offseason, Alec Bohm has emerged as a target for both clubs in free agency.
articles.body:
With both the New York Yankees and New York Mets searching for infield help this offseason, Alec Bohm has emerged as a target for both clubs in free agency.

Per The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , officials from both New York clubs have met with Bohm's representatives this week at the general managers' meetings in Las Vegas.

Bohm has spent his entire career with the Philadelphia Phillies to this point. He was originally drafted by the team in 2018, made his MLB debut in 2020 and was an All-Star in 2024.

Even though Bohm has primarily played third base, he has 166 games of experience at first base. He moved from the hot corner to first for the final two months of the 2026 season after the Phillies acquired Luis Arraez.

Bo Bichette, who used his $42 million opt-in clause for 2027, is penciled in as the Mets' starting third baseman. Jared Young hit well playing primarily first base for them last season, but he could also handle DH duties with Jorge Polanco coming off an injury-plagued 2026.

The Yankees' primary infield need is at third base with Ryan McMahon struggling to hit since being acquired midway through the 2025 season from the Colorado Rockies.

Bohm would fit as a potential platoon role at first base for the Yankees when he is not starting at third if they want to bring Paul Goldschmidt back, but they could also give Ben Rice the full-time job there in order to use Aaron Judge more at DH coming off his injury-marred season.

Yankees general manager Brian Cashman has said Giancarlo Stanton will be back with the team in 2027. He should only DH at this point in his career given how difficult it has been to keep him in the lineup due to injuries.

Bohm is coming off one of the worst offensive seasons of his career with a .249/.315/.383 slash line in 155 games, but he closed the year strong with a .305/.383/.424 line in 177 plate appearances from Aug. 1 through Sept. 27.

At 30 years old, Bohm is still in the middle of his prime and could be a strong buy-low candidate for a team like the Yankees or Mets since they already have the star power at the top of their lineup and need more depth behind those players.

articles.title: Junior Caminero's agent tries to dunk on MLB owners amid pending lockout with brand deal compensation argument
articles.summary: Junior Caminero's agent says adidas paid the star more than the Tampa Bay Rays did, taking aim at Major League Baseball owners before a lockout.
articles.body: Major League Baseball owners are set to lock out their players if there is not a new collective bargaining agreement by Dec. 1, and an agent used the negotiations as an attempt to dunk on them. Rafael Nieves of Republik Sports represents Tampa Bay Rays star Junior Caminero, who will become a very rich man one day — in 366 career games, he already has 94 home runs. Caminero already makes plenty of money, which was the focus around Nieves' jab at owners. Nieves said most of his money earned is actually through his endorsement deal with adidas. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "I want to let people know, as we prepare for the lockout, that adidas paid Junior Caminero more money than the Tampa Bay Rays this season," Nieves posted on X on Wednesday night. The Rays are hardly known for being big spenders — their $110 million payroll ranked 29th in baseball, and they've given out only two nine-figure contracts, one of which went to Wander Franco, who is out of the league and on unpaid leave after having an inappropriate relationship with a minor. BREWERS' JACOB MISIOROWSKI, YANKEES' CAM SCHLITTLER NAMED UNANIMOUS CY YOUNG AWARD WINNERS FOR 2026 MLB SEASON But for what it's worth, this should hardly be surprising, and it probably would not matter which team he played for. Caminero is not even arbitration-eligible , so his salary this season was the league minimum of $760,000. He'll make the league minimum next year, as well, and is not slated to become a free agent until after the 2030 season. Caminero did get an additional $1 million last year from his success in his first full season when he hit 45 homers and drove in 110 runs. He figures to get a bigger bump this year after a 42-101 campaign when he slashed .276/.360/.524 that put him as an American League MVP finalist. MLB players are aiming to raise minimum salaries and avoid having a salary cap, which owners have offered for the first time since 1994 - that year's postseason was canceled, and baseball did not return until late April 1995 due to the players' strike. articles.title: New MLB Rumors on Teruaki Sato's Top Landing Spots as Scouts Compare Star to Munetaka Murakami
articles.summary: The market for Japanese star Teruaki Sato continues to fill out with a new American League suitor entering the mix.
articles.body:
The market for Japanese star Teruaki Sato continues to fill out with a new American League suitor entering the mix.

Per The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , the Texas Rangers have expressed an interest in Sato after he was posted by the Hanshin Tigers on Nov. 1.

The Rangers join a group that includes the New York Yankees, Los Angeles Dodgers, Philadelphia Phillies, New York Mets, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres as clubs believed to have some level of interest in Sato.

Sato's game has been compared in many ways to Chicago White Sox slugger Munetaka Murakami, who was the biggest NPB star posted last year after a terrific eight-season run with the Tokyo Yakult Swallows.

Per Sammon, Cody Stavenhagen and Patrick Mooney of The Athletic, scouts were particularly effusive about Sato's power which one talent evaluator graded as 70 raw.

For perspective, Murakami was viewed as having 80-grade raw power. He was able to translate that to 35 homers in his rookie year with the White Sox.

Sato, like Murakami, has had high strikeout rates in NPB. He has struck out at least 137 times in each of his six seasons with the Tigers, including a total of 327 over the past two years.

The Athletic story noted scouts view Sato as having "less swing-and-miss" than Murakami, but some evaluators "greatly prefer" the latter's swing because of how Sato sets up in the box:

"Unlike Murakami, Sato is less open with his stance and setup, somewhat parallel to the pitcher. Some who have studied Sato wonder if he's going to get tied up against lefties. That didn't happen in Japan, but he was not facing the same kind of hard-throwing pitchers."

Sato's accolades in NPB are very similar to Murakami. Both players won the triple crown — Murakami in 2022, Sato in 2026. Murakami won two Central League MVP awards in 2021 and 2022; Sato won one in 2025.

Murakami's peak years in NPB were better than Sato's. He had three years with an OPS over 1.000. Sato's single-season career-high in OPS was .991, done in 2026.

Due to questions teams had about Murakami's bat translating to MLB, he took a cheaper-than-expected two-year deal worth $34 million from the White Sox.

Murakami hit .207/.347/.478 in 127 games during the 2026 season. Even though the batting average was low and strikeouts were high (196 in 553 plate appearances), the on-base and power skills easily translated against MLB pitching.

Sato will likely benefit from Murakami's success because MLB clubs can point to what he did and feel comfortable that someone with a similar skill set is going to be able to step in as a valuable contributor right away.

articles.title: New Jazz Chisholm Jr. Rumors Update Interest Level for Yankees Star in 2026 MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: More than a third of MLB teams have spoken with Jazz Chisholm Jr. since the expiration of his previous contract with the New York Yankees, according to MLB Network's Jon Morosi.
articles.body:
More than a third of MLB teams have spoken with Jazz Chisholm Jr. since the expiration of his previous contract with the New York Yankees, according to MLB Network's Jon Morosi.

Chisholm's representatives have spoken with 11 teams and scheduled "multiple in-person meetings" for next week, according to Morosi.

The Yankees declined to extend a qualifying offer to Chisholm after he slashed .231/.312/.399 in his second full season with the club.

Chisholm has already been connected to the Toronto Blue Jays, who Sportsnet's Shi Davidi reported met Wednesday with Chisholm's camp.

Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins previously confirmed he plans to add to his offense this offseason, and Ernie Clement's position as the Blue Jays starting second baseman is in question heading into 2027, per MLB.com's Keegan Matheson .

According to Davidi, Chisholm also "is open to a versatile defensive role in which he moves between multiple positions, including the outfield."

MLB.com's Mark Feinsand previously named the Detroit Tigers, Los Angeles Angels, San Diego Padres and Cincinnati Reds as other potential landing spots for Chisholm.

Chisholm stole a career-high 41 bases while mostly playing second base this season but saw a drop in production from his 2025 All-Star campaign.

After posting a .242/.332/.481 slash line with 31 home runs and 31 stolen bases during his first full season since he was traded from the Miami Marlins, Chisholm avoided arbitration with the Yankees by agreeing to a $10.2 million salary ahead of the 2026 campaign.

He said shortly afterward he hoped to join the 50-50 club during his contract year, per MLB.com's Bryan Hoch .

Chisholm fell short of that goal this season and had a quiet playoffs, during which he batted .182 with zero RBI in four games before the Tampa Bay Rays swept the Yankees from the ALDS.

Whichever club signs Chisholm, potentially before the current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, will hope a change of scenery and his reported willingness to switch defensive positions could help the two-time All-Star bounce back in 2027.
